Its detection heuristics (django imports, urlpatterns, class-based views) are self-referential here because the target is the framework source itself. Its source cues map onto the framework's own input parse layer: the WSGI environ -> WSGIRequest (request.GET/POST/COOKIES/META populated from environ, request.headers via HttpHeaders) and the QueryDict parser; request-state reads and handler parameters in contrib.admin / contrib.auth / generic views are the framework code that consumes them. inputBoundaryInventory.summary: This audit target is the framework layer, so input boundaries are the framework's own parse points, not application endpoints: (1) the WSGI HTTP surface - django/core/handlers/wsgi.py WSGIRequest.__init__ (environ['REQUEST_METHOD'], environ.get('CONTENT_TYPE'), self.environ['wsgi.input'], get_bytes_from_wsgi(self.environ, 'QUERY_STRING')) and django/http/request.py HttpHeaders.__init__/QueryDict.__init__ turn the raw environ into request.META/GET/POST/headers; downstream framework code that consumes request state sits in contrib.admin (39 reads in options.py, 6 in views/main.py: ChangeList collects dict(request.GET.items()) at :70, the search query request.GET.get(SEARCH_VAR) at :80 and the ORDER_VAR ordering at :370-393), contrib.auth views, generic views (self.request/self.kwargs), middleware (csrf: 16 request reads, common, sessions, auth) and views/i18n/debug; (2) the CLI surface of django management commands (add_argument/options, 182/166 sites) - commands such as inspectdb, createcachetable, sqlmigrate, flush and loaddata drive the SQL layer; (3) the filesystem: open() (85 sites in django/) - template loading, file storage, translation catalogs, and loaddata fixture files (json/xml/zip content deserialized into ORM model instances); (4) the database itself: introspection table/column names and ORM values re-interpolated into PRAGMA/information_schema SQL (intermediate propagation, not external input); (5) settings/os.environ: operator-level trust (settings.DATABASES credentials consumed by backends, 465 settings.<ATTR> reads, 22 os.environ reads). The dominant SQL execution channels are the ORM compilers (cursor.execute(sql, params) in django/db/models/sql/compiler.py:1100/:1335), the central CursorWrapper (django/db/backends/utils.py:66-89 execute/executemany/callproc over driver cursors), the backend-specific cursor wrappers (sqlite3 SQLiteCursorWrapper, mysql CursorWrapper, oracle FormatStylePlaceholderCursor with _fix_for_params), the schema editor's execute (django/db/backends/base/schema.py:116, used by migrations), the GIS backends and the DB cache backend. Roughly 224 execute-family call sites exist under django/; the ORM filter()/exclude()/order_by() path used by the admin ChangeList compiles to parameterized SQL and is not modeled as a raw sink, while introspection/DDL/PRAGMA code frequently %-interpolates identifiers (quoted via quote_name) directly into the SQL text.

inputBoundaryInventory.nonVulnerabilityNote: The %-interpolated DDL/introspection SQL in the backends is driven by DB-derived table/column identifiers and settings/config values (operator/DB trust level), usually quote_name-quoted; the management-command SQL is operator CLI input; the request-derived values observed in framework code (admin ChangeList, auth views, generic views) flow into ORM filter()/order_by() channels, which compile to parameterized SQL, with the ordering index additionally int()-validated. No framework request path was observed feeding request text directly into raw SQL construction in this snapshot; all dynamic-SQL families above are recorded as candidates for the labeling step to triage, not presumed vulnerable.

match_kind ('api' = resolved real API call via API graphs, 'ast' = syntax-level match)

matchKindSemantics.api: call resolved through semmle.python.ApiGraphs; in this project NO sink or source row is expected to resolve at API level: all SQL execution flows through local cursor variables and wrapper chains that API graphs cannot bind to django.db or driver members, and the WSGI request object / environ / options / settings are framework-injected values, not module members. The column is kept for cross-project contract consistency.
matchKindSemantics.ast: pure AST shape match (attribute/name text, syntactic receiver, request/field/settings/options name conventions). All execute/executemany/callproc matches are receiver-name-agnostic (any <obj>.execute(...) matches), which tolerates cursor aliasing (cursor, self.cursor, schema_editor, wrapper chains) but cannot prove the receiver is a database cursor - name-collision noise is possible and is left to the labeling step.

extraction.expectedVolume: roughly 3500-5500 source rows (request attribute reads ~150, request .get()/.getlist()/subscript reads ~100, whole-mapping reads ~30, handler parameters ~800-1000 across 323 handler functions, WSGI environ reads ~30, cli add_argument/options/handle ~500, env ~25, file open/read ~180, config settings reads ~465, internal_transfer call args ~500-1500) and roughly 500-900 sink rows (224 execute-family call sites + bound_params companion rows + construction nodes inside SQL wrapper functions + wrapper function rows + ~30 sql_api_def rows). This is in line with prior projects in this series (maltrail 617/52, pgadmin4 2150/61, arches ~1500-2500/~200-400).

uncoveredCases: Positional-argument scan cap: the environ-receiving-call family and the internal_transfer family enumerate argument positions 0-9 (i is bound by range membership before the indexed Call.getPositionalArg(i) lookup, because the index parameter of getPositionalArg is a checked/total-function input in QL); calls with more than 10 positional arguments would not be scanned. No such call was observed on the SQL-relevant paths in this snapshot.

request.body / request.headers: neither has read sites in non-test framework code (request.headers property defined at django/http/request.py:71 but unused); no http_body family and no header-specific family were emitted. request.user / request.method / request.path / request.LANGUAGE_CODE are framework-computed or container state and are not emitted.

Handler detection is name- and position-based: functions whose request parameter is not named `request` (or CBV methods where it is not at position 1) are not captured; middleware __call__(self, request) IS captured (it is a genuine request boundary).

QueryDict accessor methods beyond .get/.getlist/.items/.copy/.urlencode (keys(), values(), lists(), pop(), setlist(), iteration) are not emitted as separate families; `PAGE_VAR in request.GET` containment checks are Compare nodes and are not captured.
Keyword-argument hand-offs into SQL wrapper functions (e.g. any **options propagation into execute(sql, params=...)) are not captured by internal_transfer (positional arguments only).

Direct .execute(...) call sites are modeled as sink rows, not as internal_transfer rows: callsSqlWrapper deliberately excludes wrapper functions named execute/executemany/callproc so the same call site is not double-modeled as a transfer.

Variable-template %-formatting (sql % {...} / sql % tuple(...) where the template is a variable, e.g. django/db/backends/base/schema.py:132/:796/:826, oracle/operations.py:412, sqlite3/operations.py:155, models/constraints.py:40/:86, models/indexes.py:68, models/sql/query.py:119/:266) is NOT captured by the construction family (which requires a literal template on the left of %); these sites are still represented by their execute rows and listed in detection.json dynamicSqlSites.

Cross-function construction (SQL built in one function, executed in another) is not traced at extraction time; the construction family only covers constructions directly executed as argument 0 or located inside a function that directly executes SQL.

Dynamic receiver identity: <obj>.execute(...) matching is syntactic; whether the receiver is a django.db cursor, a driver cursor or an unrelated object with an execute method is not resolved. In this snapshot every .execute( site found by grep in django/ is a database cursor, but the query tolerates collisions by design.

Manager.raw()/Manager.extra(): QuerySet methods are copied onto Manager at runtime (django/db/models/manager.py); no def sites exist on Manager, so sql_api_def rows cover the QuerySet definitions only - Manager-side call sites in downstream applications would rely on the QuerySet rows plus label-time aliasing.

GIS backends (django/contrib/gis/db/backends/*) are covered by the same AST-level execute-member and construction shapes; spatial SQL function construction in base/operations.py:91-102 mixes %-formatted identifiers with preserved %%s bound placeholders - the construction row and the bound channel are emitted from the same expression only when shapes match.

Django ORM model-manager calls (filter()/exclude()/order_by()/Q) and the URL router (django/urls) are framework-internal and not extracted; the ORM raw channels are covered as sql_api_def definitions instead of call sites (no .raw()/.extra()/RawSQL() call sites exist in non-test framework code).
Fixture deserialization (loaddata) and file-content flows are captured as file rows (open/.read) but the file-content -> ORM -> SQL data flow is not traced at extraction time.

Compile/runtime validation of both queries is deferred with execution: per the task contract, CodeQL was not invoked in this round (no query run, no bqrs decode, no query compile). The queries reuse the exact structural shapes (helpers, bindingset annotations, AST-cast matching, no QL classes, moduleHint naming) that compiled and ran clean against CodeQL CLI 2.25.1 + codeql/python-all 7.1.x in the arches CWE-89 run of this series.
